svg.text: The Technology Stack Beneath Bitcoin
Each layer is enabled by the one below and secured by it. Identifiers (L0–L5, T-xx) match the companion report.
BITCOIN · 2008–09
New: Nakamoto consensus (T-13) · difficulty adjustment (T-18) · closed PoW↔issuance incentive loop
Reused: everything below
L5 · DIGITAL-CASH DESIGN
problem solved: double-spend without an issuer
T-19 Blind signatures / eCash — Chaum 1982, DigiCash 1990–98 (anonymity, but central bank)
T-20 Cypherpunks — Hughes, May, Gilmore 1992 (agenda + community)
T-21 b-money — Wei Dai 1998 (shared ledger kept by all) · T-22 bit gold — Szabo 1998/2005 (PoW chain)
T-16 RPOW — Finney 2004 (PoW as transferable token) · T-23 e-gold / Liberty Reserve (central = shut down)
T-24 Double-spend problem — open until Bitcoin fixes transaction ORDER via L2+L3+L4
L4 · ECONOMIC / ANTI-ABUSE MECHANISMS
problem solved: cost to participate; incentive to behave
T-14 Proof-of-work as pricing — Dwork & Naor 1992 (anti-spam)
T-15 Hashcash — Adam Back 1997/2002 (find nonce → leading-zero hash; Bitcoin mining = this + SHA-256)
T-17 Incentive-compatible protocols — BitTorrent tit-for-tat 2001; mechanism design
T-18 Difficulty adjustment — Bitcoin 2009 (feedback control on block time)
L3 · DISTRIBUTED AGREEMENT
problem solved: distrusting nodes agree on one history
T-11 Byzantine Generals — Lamport, Shostak, Pease 1982 (<1/3 faulty) · FLP impossibility 1985
T-12 PBFT — Castro & Liskov 1999 (practical, but needs KNOWN members)
T-03 Sybil attack — Douceur 2002 (open networks can't count identities → why PoW is needed)
T-13 Nakamoto consensus — 2008 (heaviest-work chain; open membership; probabilistic finality)
L2 · AUTHENTICATED DATA STRUCTURES
problem solved: tamper-evident ordering & membership
T-08 Merkle trees — Merkle 1979 (one root commits to many items; log-size proofs → SPV)
T-09 Linked timestamping — Haber & Stornetta 1991; + Merkle 1992; Surety NYT anchoring 1995
T-10 "Chain of blocks" = T-09 + T-08 + T-15 (hash-linked headers, each costly to extend)
L1 · CRYPTOGRAPHIC PRIMITIVES
problem solved: ownership, integrity, unforgeability
T-04 Public-key crypto — Diffie–Hellman 1976; RSA 1977 (first practical digital signature)
T-06 Elliptic curves — Koblitz/Miller 1985; ECDSA 1992→2000; secp256k1 (SEC 2, 2000)
T-07 Hash functions — Merkle 1979; MD5 1992; SHA-1 1995; RIPEMD-160 1996; SHA-256 2001
T-05 Signature security definition — Goldwasser, Micali, Rivest 1988
L0 · COMMUNICATION SUBSTRATE
problem solved: nodes find and talk to each other
T-01 TCP/IP — Cerf & Kahn 1974; ARPANET cut-over 1983 (untrusted, best-effort transport)
T-02 P2P overlays — Napster 1999; Gnutella 2000 (gossip flood); BitTorrent 2001; Kademlia 2002
Bitcoin uses: plain TCP :8333, gossip propagation, DNS seeds — all security pushed up to L1–L4
enables ↑ · secured by ↓
Timeline
grey = post-Bitcoin evolution
Digital-cash lineage: what each attempt solved and what it left open

g.text: No issuer: PoW issues coins (subsidy) · No trusted registry: every node holds the chain
Conflicts resolved: heaviest-work chain fixes transaction order → first-buried spend wins
Sybil-proof: one CPU, one vote · Self-funding: the work that secures the ledger is paid in the ledger's own unit
